paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The average probing accuracy using different MLP variations. We indicate the size(s) of hidden layer(s) in square brackets.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates average probing accuracy differences (expressed as percentage-point difference) for two multilingual models across several MLP probing-head variations defined by hidden-layer size(s) and activation. The horizontal axis contains four categorical configurations in left-to-right order: “hidden:[50], linear,” “hidden:[], linear,” “hidden:[100], ReLU,” and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU.” The vertical axis is labeled “% point difference” and uses a linear scale with labeled ticks at approximately −0.2, −0.1, 0.0, 0.1, and 0.2, spanning roughly from −0.2 to a little above 0.2. Each category shows a grouped pair of bars, with mBERT shown in a light blue bar and XLM-R shown in a darker blue bar (legend in the upper right). For “hidden:[50], linear,” the mBERT bar extends to about −0.20 and the XLM-R bar to about −0.06. For “hidden:[], linear,” mBERT is around +0.09 and XLM-R is around +0.21 (the tallest positive bar). For “hidden:[100], ReLU,” mBERT is around −0.12 while XLM-R is around +0.03. For “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” mBERT is around −0.18 and XLM-R is around −0.14. The bars are not visually annotated or otherwise emphasized beyond the consistent color coding and side-by-side grouping within each category, and the category order appears to follow the listed configurations rather than an explicit sorting by value.
